summary: Planetary Twin Finder is an interactive web tool that finds places on Earth with terrain similar to selected sites on the Moon or Mars. Our team developed it to make the search for terrestrial analogs faster and more consistent. The tool divides planetary maps into 5 × 5 km tiles, represents each tile with a 128-number fingerprint based on terrain and surface properties, and uses FAISS to search an index of 575,483 Earth tiles. Users can choose a lunar or Martian site, view the closest Earth matches on a map, and compare terrain features in side-by-side visualizations. By making it easier to identify and inspect candidate sites, Planetary Twin Finder can support rover testing, instrument trials, and crew training on Earth before future missions.
details: Planetary Twin Finder is a web tool developed by Astra Frontier to find places on Earth with terrain similar to selected sites on the Moon or Mars. It replaces time-consuming manual map searches with a repeatable process. Users select a target site, receive a ranked list of Earth analogs, and compare the features behind each match. We used Copernicus elevation data for Earth, NASA’s LOLA and Diviner data for the Moon, and MOLA elevation data for Mars. Using pyproj, we divided the maps into 5 × 5 km tiles of consistent size, including near the poles, and resampled them to 64 × 64 grids. Each tile includes five layers covering slope, roughness, relative relief, thermal inertia, and aridity or albedo. Relative relief lets us compare landforms across planets with different elevation reference systems. Inspired by audio fingerprinting, our GeoAutoencoder compresses each tile into a 128-number fingerprint without manually labeled examples. The model is designed to recognize similar terrain at different orientations. FAISS uses cosine similarity to search 575,483 Earth tiles. The website displays a global similarity heatmap and lets users inspect matches through side-by-side 3D views, surface layers, terrain cross-sections, and fingerprint comparisons. Planetary Twin Finder could help mission teams shortlist field sites for rover testing, instrument trials, and crew training. For example, a rover team could compare slope and roughness across candidate sites before deciding where to conduct field tests.
